title: Signature Mail Shield
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Mail Shield is Manon's original design for a mail gate that refuses to trust a sender name until independent checks confirm it. The design treats every inbound message as a stranger making a claim: the claimed domain must match the domain the message actually came from, the message must carry valid sender authentication, and any link inside must point where its text says it points. A message failing any of these is quarantined, not delivered with a warning the reader must interpret, because the design's premise is that warnings do not stop deception while quarantine does. The shield is a gate, not a filter with opinions: it admits only mail that proves itself.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The shield recognizes deception by the same tells defenders already know: lookalike domains, urgency language, mismatched link destinations, unexpected attachments, and requests for passwords or codes. Its awareness layer records every quarantined message with the exact failed check, so the defended organization learns which lures are aimed at it and can warn staff with real examples instead of generic advice. The design also tracks reporting: when a reader reports a message the shield admitted, that message's checks are reviewed and the rule is tightened, so the shield learns from its misses in the open instead of hiding them.

SOLUTIONS. The shield's cure is its gate rule: authenticate, match, and quarantine on failure, with no delivery of failed mail to inboxes. Its immunization is its own-domain publishing: the defended organization's domains publish strict authentication so other gates can verify its mail too. Its fix playbook runs automatically on a reported wave: quarantine the wave's messages across all inboxes, revoke sessions for anyone who submitted credentials, and force resets. Resistance verification: the shield's demo runs labeled samples through its gate and requires every deceptive sample quarantined and every legitimate sample admitted before the gate is trusted.

title: Signature Message Voice Guard
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Message Voice Guard is Manon's original design for a guard that sits between an inbound text or call and any action it requests. The guard scores every message on three signals: urgency that forbids checking, impersonation of a trusted party, and a request to tap, call back, or read a code. Two or more signals quarantine the message and present the reader with a single instruction: do not comply, verify through a channel you already trust. For calls, the guard's rule is simpler and stricter: any inbound call requesting codes, access, or payment is refused, and the caller is told to use a published channel. The guard assumes the caller ID is meaningless, because it is.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The guard recognizes deception by collecting the lures aimed at its users: sender numbers, link domains, and scripts are logged with their scores, so repeated waves are visible as patterns rather than isolated complaints. Its awareness output is a plain-language warning carrying the exact lure text, so staff learn the current wave rather than last year's examples. The design also watches for the quiet signal of a successful attack: a sudden request for a verification code the user did not initiate, which the guard treats as evidence that someone is already trying to enter an account.

SOLUTIONS. The guard's cure is its quarantine rule: scored messages never reach the user as actionable requests. Its immunization is its training loop: every quarantined wave becomes a training example shown to staff with its tells labeled. Its fix playbook on a reported wave blocks the sender and domain, warns the targeted group with the exact text, and reviews accounts for compliance. title: Signature Password Fortress
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Password Fortress is Manon's original design for making stolen passwords useless. Its rule has three walls: every password must be long, every password must be unique to one service, and every important account must require a second factor the password cannot satisfy. The design treats a password as a first key only: it opens nothing important alone. A password manager is part of the design, not an optional extra, because long unique passwords are only practical when a tool remembers them. The fortress also rejects known breached and common passwords at creation, so a user cannot choose a password that is already public.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The fortress recognizes weakness by testing every password against length, variety, breach lists, and reuse, and it reports weakness in plain language instead of a cryptic score. Its awareness layer watches sign-in patterns for credential-stuffing shape: many accounts tried from few sources, or one account tried from many places, and it raises the second-factor requirement when that shape appears. The design treats every breach notice as a fortress event: the breached password is marked, every account reusing it is flagged, and the user is guided through changing them in order of importance, starting with mail.

SOLUTIONS. The fortress's cure is its creation rule: long, unique, and breach-checked, or the password is refused. Its immunization is the second factor on every important account, which means a leaked password alone opens nothing. Its fix playbook on a breach revokes sessions, forces changes in importance order, and verifies the new passwords meet the rule. Resistance verification: the fortress's demo runs sample passwords through its policy and requires every weak or reused sample rejected and every strong unique sample accepted before the policy is trusted.

title: Signature Port Guard
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Port Guard is Manon's original design for a port policy that treats every inserted device as untrusted until proven otherwise. The guard disables automatic execution from removable media entirely, admits only devices whose hardware identifiers are registered, and scans admitted media before any file is opened. An unregistered device is not merely warned about; it is blocked at the port, and the attempt is logged with the machine, the time, and the device identifier. The design's premise is that a user cannot safely inspect an unknown device, so the system must make the unsafe action impossible rather than asking the user to judge it.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The guard recognizes risk by logging every insertion attempt, admitted or blocked, so an organization sees which machines face the most attempts and whether attempts cluster around events or visitors. Its awareness output names the blocked identifiers, which lets security teams spot a repeated device trying many machines, the signature of a deliberate campaign rather than a lost drive. The design also watches for the quiet failure mode: a registered device used on a machine outside its approved set, which the guard treats as a policy violation worth review even though the device itself is known.

SOLUTIONS. The guard's cure is its port rule: unregistered means blocked, with no override at the machine. Its immunization is its registration process: devices are registered only through an approved request naming an owner and a purpose, and registrations expire. Its fix playbook on a blocked-device incident preserves logs, scans the machine, and checks for new programs or tasks before the machine returns to service. Resistance verification: the guard's demo runs sample devices through its policy and requires every unregistered device blocked and every registered, scanned device admitted before the policy is trusted.

title: Signature Patch Sentinel
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Patch Sentinel is Manon's original design for a watcher that never lets a system quietly fall behind its fixes. The sentinel keeps an inventory of every program on every machine, watches vendor advisories for those programs, and compares installed versions against fixed versions continuously rather than at audit time. A system below a fixed version is marked exposed, with the exposure age counted in days, and internet-facing systems are marked urgent first. The design's premise is that patching fails not from ignorance of the fix but from invisibility of the gap, so the sentinel makes the gap visible, counted, and owned.

The sentinel recognizes exposure by version arithmetic and by advisory matching, and it reports exposure as a list with owners and ages, not as a percentage that hides which machines are behind. Its awareness layer also watches for the exploitation window: when a critical advisory lands, it starts a clock for every affected system and escalates systems that pass the deadline without a fix or a documented workaround. The design treats a workaround as a temporary shield with an expiry, not as a resolution, so workarounds cannot silently become permanent.

title: Signature Airwave Shield
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Airwave Shield is Manon's original design for a connection rule that never trusts a network it does not control. The shield judges every connection on two facts: is the traffic itself encrypted, and is the network trusted. A connection is allowed for sensitive work only when its traffic is encrypted and either the network is trusted or a private tunnel carries the traffic. An open network with encrypted traffic and a tunnel passes; an open network with plain traffic fails; a shared-password network without a tunnel fails for sensitive work, because a shared password does not make traffic private from other users of the same network. The shield enforces the rule in software, so the user never has to judge a network by its name.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The shield recognizes risk by logging connection decisions with their reasons, so an organization sees which networks its people actually use and which ones keep failing the rule. The gate distributes the service across locations, rate-limits per source and per request type, caches aggressively at the edge, and hands the largest floods to an upstream provider built for them. Slow attacks that hold connections open are met with timeouts, so resources cannot be held without volume. The design's premise is that availability is a security property: a service that cannot answer its users has failed them just as surely as a service that leaked their data.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. The flood gate recognizes floods by traffic shape, not only totals: surges uncorrelated with real events, half-open connection floods, and one expensive request type dominating load all look different from a genuine crowd. Its awareness layer reports traffic shape continuously, so the difference between a crowd and a flood is visible before users time out. The design also watches for the quiet variant: slow-rate attacks that exhaust without volume, which totals-based monitoring misses entirely.

SOLUTIONS. The flood gate's cure is its layered defense: distribution, rate limits, edge caching, and contracted upstream mitigation in place before it is needed. Its immunization is its timeout and shedding policy: expensive request types are shed first, and connections cannot be held indefinitely. Its fix playbook on a flood confirms it is not a real surge, applies rate limits and upstream filtering, sheds expensive types first, and communicates status to users. title: Signature Egress Watch

EDUCATION. The Signature Egress Watch is Manon's original design for watching what leaves, by whom, and to where. The watch records every egress of sensitive data with its user, volume, time, and destination, and it flags patterns that break baseline: bulk transfers before a resignation, access outside a role, off-hours movement, and uploads to personal storage. The design's premise is that insider misuse looks like work until its pattern breaks, so the watch looks for broken patterns rather than forbidden tools. Least privilege and separation of duties stand behind the watch: the watch detects, while narrow permissions limit what any one person can take.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. Egress Watch recognizes risk by baselines per user and per role, so a transfer is judged against that person's normal behavior rather than a single global threshold. Its awareness layer reports anomalies with full context, volume, time, destination, and role fit, so reviewers can judge quickly instead of drowning in alerts. The design treats a resignation notice as a watch event: access is reviewed before departure, not after, and bulk movement in the notice window triggers immediate review. The watch also guards its own logs: log tampering is itself an alert, because an insider who understands monitoring attacks the monitor first.

SOLUTIONS. Egress Watch's cure is its pattern detection with baselines and role fit. Its immunization is least privilege, separation of duties, and prompt revocation when roles change or people leave. Its fix playbook on suspected misuse preserves logs before confronting anyone, suspends affected access through proper channels, determines what left and where it went, and closes the access path that made it possible. title: Signature Face-Voice Check
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Face-Voice Check is Manon's original design for a rule that no voice or face alone authorizes anything consequential. Every sensitive instruction delivered by voice or video must be verified through an independent channel: a call back on a known number, a confirmation in writing through a separate system, or a pre-shared code word the impersonator does not know. The design treats recognition as identification only: recognizing a voice says who it sounds like, while authorization requires proof through a channel the impersonator does not control. A familiar voice is therefore never sufficient, even when it is the chief executive's voice, because familiarity is exactly what synthesis reproduces.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. Face-Voice Check recognizes risk by its context: urgent voice or video instructions to move money or share credentials, calls from unexpected numbers, audio that sounds right but slightly flat, and refusals to confirm in writing. Its awareness layer records every refused voice instruction with its scenario, so staff learn the current impersonation scripts rather than last year's. The design also watches for the quiet signal of a campaign: several staff receiving similar voice instructions in a short window, which indicates a targeted operation rather than isolated pranks.

Its immunization is its code-word system: sensitive approvals carry pre-shared words that change on a schedule, so a recorded voice from last month cannot authorize this month's payment. Its fix playbook on a reported attempt freezes the requested action, warns the targeted team with the exact scenario, preserves the recording, and adds the scenario to training. title: Signature Browse Shield
body:
EDUCATION. The Signature Browse Shield is Manon's original design for a browser that treats every site, including familiar ones, as potentially compromised. The shield patches promptly, blocks scripts and plugins by default except on an allowlist of trusted sites, and separates browsing for sensitive work from general web use, so a compromised general site cannot reach sensitive sessions. A watering hole works by compromising a site the victims already visit; the shield answers by making the visit itself harmless, since the trap needs script execution or a download the shield does not permit. The design's premise is that visiting is not consenting: a browser should not run a stranger's code at full power merely because its owner visited a page.

INFORMATION AWARENESS. Browse Shield recognizes risk by watching for the symptoms of a successful drive-by: unexpected downloads, new extensions, changed home pages, and outbound connections after visits to specific sites. Its awareness layer logs which sites requested script execution and which were denied, so a newly compromised trusted site shows up as a change in behavior rather than remaining invisible. The design also treats a familiar site requesting a new permission or download as an event worth review, because familiar sites are the watering hole's lure.

SOLUTIONS. Browse Shield's cure is its default-deny script and plugin policy with a narrow allowlist. Its immunization is its separation: sensitive work browses in a separate profile or isolated environment from general use. Its fix playbook on a suspected drive-by isolates the machine, removes unknown extensions and downloads, scans fully, checks for persistence, and reviews what the browser could reach.
